title: Tango: A Cross-layer Approach to Managing I/O Interference over Local Ephemeral Storage
problem: Multiple applications sharing local ephemeral storage (NVMe, die-stacked memory, burst buffers) in non-exclusive node usage scenarios experience I/O interference that degrades analytics performance. Existing methods like in situ processing cannot support diverse analytics needs that emerge late in post-processing when data interference patterns are unknown.
motivation: Exascale scientific discovery requires minimizing time to knowledge for post-processing analytics while managing complex storage hierarchies with multiple interference-inducing applications.
method: Tango uses a coordinated cross-layer approach where the application layer decomposes and distributes analysis data across the storage hierarchy, reducing or avoiding lower-tier access during high interference while maintaining prescribed error bounds. The storage layer couples this with adaptive bandwidth allocation decisions based on augmentation cardinality, accuracy requirements, and application characteristics.
key_novelty: Coordinated cross-layer adaptation that couples application-driven data distribution with storage-layer bandwidth management to dynamically react to I/O interference while maintaining analytics accuracy.
contributions: Cross-layer framework for managing I/O interference in shared ephemeral storage across multiple applications
Adaptive data distribution mechanism that maintains prescribed error bounds while avoiding high-interference storage tiers
Storage-layer bandwidth allocation strategy based on augmentation properties and application characteristics
Quantitative evaluation showing 52% improvement over no adaptivity and 36% over single-layer adaptivity on real HPC workloads

metrics.speedup: 52% vs no adaptivity, 36% vs single-layer adaptivity
metrics.accuracy: maintains acceptable analytics outcomes with prescribed error bound

primary_theme: adaptive I/O interference management for exascale data analytics
